clue.text: Leader of Conservatives blocking change leads to dispute

indicators.note: the leader stands in the way of the change by sitting inside it

parts.note: an alteration is a change

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter of Conservatives is used

explanation.surface: A senior Tory obstructing reform causes a political row.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel, so it is a dispute.

clue.text: A small flat is fitting

definitions.meaning: the standard abbreviation for an apartment, a small way of writing flat

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line that a compact apartment is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable; it is also the short written form of apartment, a flat.

clue.text: G-string aria for one with a lisp

indicators.note: someone with a lisp says a th sound where an s should be, so that swap is made

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A stripper's garment is an operatic number as mispronounced by a lisper.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy undergarment, another name for a G-string.

clue.text: Deodorants applied during bowls

indicators.note: the applied part falls within the bowling, so it goes inside

parts.note: to bowl a ball is to roll it, so bowls means rolls
a cream that is applied is on the skin

explanation.surface: Players put on antiperspirant in the middle of a game of bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Roll-ons are deodorants dispensed by a rolling ball applicator.

clue.text: A little application and skill used to make dessert

indicators.note: only a little of the word application is kept, its first four letters

parts.note: et is French and Latin for and
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A recipe note: some effort and craft go into making a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple tart is a classic pastry pudding served after the main course.

clue.text: Intimate spotted taking a pee

indicators.note: taking away the letter leaves the rest of the word

parts.note: pimply skin is spotted with pimples
pee is the spelt-out name of the letter P

explanation.surface: A close friend with acne is caught relieving themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate something is to suggest it indirectly, to hint at it.

clue.text: Maybe almond covering for fruitcake

parts.note: an almond is an example of a nut
a case is a protective covering

explanation.surface: A baker considers using almond as the shell for a fruit cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, as is nutcase.

clue.text: Cricket side jeer, opening pair having been dismissed

indicators.note: in cricket the openers are the first two batsmen; here the first two letters of the word are sent away

parts.note: to scoff is to jeer or mock

explanation.surface: Fielders mock the batsmen after both openers are out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's two sides of the field are the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat.

clue.text: Extra doctor back is what attracts interest

parts.note: over means in excess, extra
aft is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An additional physician is the one who draws attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank charges interest on an overdraft, the money borrowed beyond the balance.

clue.text: I foster spring breaks without golf

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rearranged
the letter is left out of the word spring

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A self-portrait of someone who nurtures a fresh season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes G from SPRING, and 'breaks' rearranges FOSTER plus SPRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun I is the grammatical first person singular.

clue.text: Point about much reduced page is so long

indicators.note: the point wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a tip is a point, as of a pencil

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: oodles means a great deal, much

explanation.surface: A tip about a heavily shortened page is that it is quite lengthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much reduced' reads as one phrase, but 'much' gives the word and 'reduced' drops its final S; 'about' wraps the point round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is an old-fashioned British farewell, like saying goodbye.

clue.text: Affluent heiresses, in reduced circumstances, becoming possessive

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase, which is cut down to a small part of itself

explanation.surface: Rich heiresses fallen on hard times grow greedy and clingy.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'Affluent' and the start of 'heiresses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is a possessive pronoun or determiner, showing ownership by them.

clue.text: Scoundrel climbed for wild plant

parts.note: a dog is an old term for a rotten fellow
rose means went up, climbed

explanation.surface: A villain clambered up to reach a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing rose of hedgerows.

clue.text: Simultaneously accepting opposing beliefs, possibly both unliked

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Holding contradictory views might leave one disliked by both camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell coined the term in Nineteen Eighty-Four for holding two contradictory beliefs at once.

clue.text: Ready to change a long time ago

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their order

explanation.surface: Someone eager for reform, long since.
explanation.definitionFit: Since the year dot is a British idiom for since the very distant past.

clue.text: Cats with second cast for addicts

indicators.note: cast here means thrown off, so those letters go

parts.note: mousers are cats that catch mice
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A theatre note: the feline cast includes a replacement understudy for the junkies.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug users are people dependent on substances, i.e. addicts.

clue.text: Former auditor spoken of in the Treasury

indicators.note: spoken signals that the letters are said, not written

parts.note: ex means former and an auditor is a checker of accounts

explanation.surface: An ex-accountant is mentioned in a government finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exchequer is Britain's government department in charge of public money.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the Exchequer is the national treasury, the state's revenue account.

clue.text: Get garage rebuilt for a sum

indicators.note: the letters are taken apart and built up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets a garage reconstructed for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a total formed by adding things together.

clue.text: Who's greeted a gismo's introduction with excitement?

definitions.text: Who's greeted a gismo's introduction with excitement?

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter of gismo's is used
excited letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about who would greet the launch of a new device with glee.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadgeteer is a lover of gadgets, who welcomes any new gizmo eagerly.

clue.text: Rent boy hanging around church with speed

indicators.note: the boy is placed round the other letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy
CE is the Church of England
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A rent boy lingers near a church, moving fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is not landlord's money but past tense of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as the past participle of rend means torn, as is lacerated.

clue.text: American in residence supplying drilling tools

indicators.note: the American goes inside the residence

parts.note: Amer is short for American

explanation.surface: A US resident provides the equipment for boring holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reamers are tools that enlarge or finish drilled holes.

clue.text: Heads for starters

definitions.meaning: the tops of skulls, especially bald ones
pâtés are spreads often served as first courses

explanation.surface: Heads served for starters, as at a gruesome banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pates are heads; pâtés are meat pastes eaten as a first course.

clue.text: 27 served up in pop is something spicy

indicators.note: the turned drink goes inside father

parts.note: pop and papa are both words for father

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: the answer to clue 27 across, a wine-and-cassis drink

explanation.surface: A cocktail offered inside a soft drink makes it fiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a spice ground from dried red peppers.

clue.text: Bums are on view from behind in eg cossies

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the clothes

parts.note: cossies are swimming costumes, and togs are clothes, especially swimwear

indicators.note: seen from behind, the word reads the other way

explanation.surface: Buttocks are visible from the rear in swimsuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bums' looks like bottoms but means layabouts. 'on view from behind' reads 'are' backwards and 'in' puts it inside the swimwear; 'cossies' is British slang for swimming costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bums in the sense of layabouts or wretches are toerags, British slang for worthless people.

clue.text: Arabic work (not old) written up above

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters run upwards, reversed
not means the letter is left out

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: An Arabic text, not an ancient one, is quoted earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes O from OPUS to leave PUS; 'written up' reverses ARPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Supra is Latin for above, used in texts to refer to an earlier passage.

clue.text: Describe former flat

parts.note: ex means former
a plain is flat country

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to depict the apartment they used to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to set it out in words, to explain it.

clue.text: One's heard a sheep consumed

indicators.note: what one hears is the words said, not written

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a sheep has been eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat something up is to consume all of it.

clue.text: Without outside assistance, Head Office going to be engaged

indicators.note: those letters go, leaving the rest

parts.note: work done in-house uses a firm's own staff, with no outside help

explanation.surface: Head Office going it alone to keep busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or toilet that is engaged is occupied, in use.

clue.text: Quietly living in Cleveland, perhaps

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a resident lives in a place

explanation.surface: Someone lives discreetly in the Ohio city of Cleveland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleveland' looks like the US city; it is Grover Cleveland.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was twice US head of state, an example of a holder of that office.

clue.text: Little spirit shown by football club's front three

indicators.note: only the first three letters of the club's name are kept

parts.note: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club

explanation.surface: A football team's forward line shows little team spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club; in football a front three is a trio of strikers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, such as rum or whisky.

clue.text: One in Sweden's ready for a drink

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the currency

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and kr is the abbreviation for Sweden's krona
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Swede is prepared to have something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is an aperitif of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur.

clue.text: One may have a nap on the flight

definitions.text: One may have a nap on the flight

parts.words: One may have a nap on the flight
parts.note: nap is the raised pile of a fabric and a flight is a set of steps, not sleep on a plane

explanation.surface: A passenger dozes on an aeroplane journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpet laid on stairs has a pile, or nap, covering a flight of steps.
